angle: Movement translation, DL (clearest of five groups screened): each rusher's tracked Combine 40 start (speed every 0.1 s from first movement) laid over his own random NFL pass-rush starts from game_frames_sample on one clock; per-player Carry-over and the NFL first step tested against pressure beyond draft pick, weight and role, with rushes as exposure, out of class, under a sensitivity grid, and through a false-positive case study.
metric_name: Carry-over: NFL first step (mean speed 0.3-0.5 s after first movement on random NFL pass-rush starts, alignment-adjusted) minus Combine 40 first step, each in sd after weight and EDGE share
headline_number: After weight and role the 40 start previews the NFL first step at rho 0.07 [-0.14, 0.28] (n = 67, p 0.59); carry-over vs pressure beyond pick 0.18 [-0.10, 0.43] (n = 52). NFL first step: +0.6 pressure-rate pts per sd [0.1, 1.1] in a quasi-binomial exposure model (n = 69, p 0.04), held-out likelihood up in 3 of 3 classes; top vs bottom third beat the out-of-class forecast 14/23 vs 3/23 (one-sided Fisher 0.001), positive in 27 of 27 sensitivity cells, but the clean 2025 class went 2/7 vs 1/9 (mid-p 0.23).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_09/cand_3 (7.82), applying the round-9 judges' top_changes. (1) Lede cut to about 75 words with the key numbers and the 2025 miss. (2) Main stats table cut from 10 rows to 4; technical rows moved to an appendix table. (3) New false-positive case study (Maason Smith): best NFL first step but 3.9% vs 7.7% forecast, with interior share, quick-pressure share, NGS get-off, a sideways-movement stunt check, film cues, the cost of the wrong call in pressures per season, and a scheme caveat; Smith replaces Diaby in the hero figure. (4) Mechanism stated as an empirical correlate, backed by an in-game proxy with n: the first step tracks NGS get-off snap by snap (0.51, 1,563 starts) but relates more to late than to quick pressures (0.28 vs 0.11). (5) Per-class hit rates with one-sided Fisher and mid-p. (6) 27-cell sensitivity grid (cut-off x minimum rushes x forecast spec). (7) Quasi-binomial model with rushes as exposure plus rotation share and a pick x rotation term, held-out log-likelihood per class, and the 30-99 vs 100+ rush slopes. (8) Power statement for the 2026 prospective test. (9) The R2 dot-plot figure is replaced by a held-out calibration + sensitivity heatmap figure. (10) NGS get-off column on the decision card. 4 figures + 3 tables; 1,809 words by check.py (1,943 by wc).
open_risks: The clean 2025 class does not confirm the sort (2/7 vs 1/9, mid-p 0.23), and a single 2026 class has only 8-34% power, so the positive evidence rests on 2023-24
Held-out evidence is mixed: likelihood with rushes as exposure improves in all three classes but by small amounts, while rush-weighted R2 falls (-0.113), with 2024 dominated by Smith
Season NGS get-off already ranks pressure at 0.40 and the first step adds only 0.12 beyond it (p 0.33), so for clubs with NGS it is a tiebreak

The headline answer to the angle's question is still a null (translation adds nothing beyond pick); the first-step window was read off the payoff curve (best-of-13 p 0.13), and DL was chosen after screening five groups
The sort weakens against a pick-only forecast (gap 14-32 points), and the case-study film cues are hypotheses: there are no blockers or ball in the game sample
